correctness.rationale: The exact unrooted count F_{n,k} is obtained by decomposing at vertex 1. Cayley’s formulas and Lagrange inversion yield F_{m,2}=((m-1)(m+6)/2)m^{m-4} and H_m=(m-1)(m+6)/(2m²); the difference H_m-H_{m+1}=(m-2)(5m+3)/(2m²(m+1)²) is positive for m>=3. Therefore q_2/p_2>q_1/p_1 for every n>=5, whereas p_{n-1}>0=q_{n-1}, proving failure in both LR directions. n=3,4 are checked analytically by H_2=H_3=1 and supports. For the rooted model the weighted matrix-tree generating polynomial z(n+z)^{n-1} gives the tagged mass and a strictly decreasing adjacent-k mass ratio on its common support; endpoint cases are included. The attached exact checker independently enumerates acyclic labeled graphs through six vertices and passes 391,322 integer/fraction assertions; the all-n claim relies on the complete analytic derivations, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The putative new result is the sharp all-n unrooted-uniform likelihood-ratio incomparability for the change from two to three components, first at five vertices, contrasted with the already established root-marked monotone forest process. Pitman (1999) already supplies the exact rooted PMF and monotone coupling, so these are explicitly recognized as published and the rooted LR strengthening itself follows from that formula. Primary full-text comparisons of Pitman, Janson, Kassel–Kenyon–Wu, and Tang–Zhang, and specific semantic mathematical-finding searches uncovered no statement or stronger implication of the sharp uniform-unrooted LR failure. The inaccessible full Łuczak–Pittel paper and possible classical total-positivity implications remain genuine unresolved priority risks; absence of a database match is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Conditioning on the number of tree components is central to random-forest and additive-coalescent models. A monotone merging/deletion coupling already shows a weak ordering in the root-marked ensemble; this result resolves a more informative strong-order comparison and shows that removal of component root marks breaks the likelihood-ratio property at the smallest nontrivial forest size. The exact universal counterfamily holds for every n>=5 rather than a cherry-picked small case, and the obstruction is explained by the two-component-to-tree count ratio and an explicit strict finite difference. This model-choice boundary clarifies which kinds of monotone conditional inferences remain valid; it does not claim a general-graph extension or that LR incomparability implies stochastic incomparability.
